title: Getting Noticed Before a Word Is Spoken
heading: Getting Noticed Before a Word Is Spoken

sourceRefs.role: explicit friend-signal support and rapid rapport framing

coreClaim: People form sticky first impressions fast, so low-threat nonverbal cues matter before words can do much repair work.
distinctMechanism: Friend signals reduce perceived threat and increase approachability by broadcasting warmth and nonhostility in the first seconds of contact.
requiredAnchors: Eyebrow flash is a rapid signal that you do not pose a threat.
A head tilt reads as vulnerable and trusting rather than guarded.
Smile and related open cues help make another person more willing to engage.
specificApplications: Repairing a chilly first impression before it hardens.
commonMisreadings: Friend signals are enough by themselves.
Negative first impressions are easy to reverse.
Low-threat cues mean acting fake or submissive.
hardEdgeRequirement: Hard depth must preserve that first-impression control is useful but limited: if later words and behavior contradict the signals, the effect decays fast.
thresholdQuestion: When does managing the opening seconds of an interaction stop being respectful social intelligence and start becoming a shallow performance?
